title: How videos tell a story
outcome: Learn how a few pictures in the right order can tell a simple story.
topics: The steps of making a video
How pictures and sound work together
assignment: Watch two short videos and note how they tell their story. Then put six photos or clips in order to show an activity. Add two lines about what you want people to understand.
evidence: Someone can watch your sequence and say what happens.
checks: Someone can tell what happens from your pictures
You explain what you wanted to show and why
You noted how two videos tell their story

title: Turn an idea into a simple plan
outcome: Turn an idea into a short plan you can film.
topics: A clear start, middle and end
assignment: Write a one-page plan for your activity video. Include the topic, your main message, how long it is, the shots you need and anything people will say.
evidence: Your plan says what people will see and learn, not just the topic.
checks: Your plan has a topic, one message and a viewer
It says what people will see, not just the topic
The length and shots are easy to film

title: Get ready for a shoot
outcome: Plan a small shoot with a shot list and a checklist.
topics: Checking light and noise where you film
Asking people before you film them
assignment: Make a list of 6 to 10 shots, a gear checklist and a simple schedule. Ask permission from anyone you will film. Record a short test, copy it to your computer and check it plays.
evidence: You are ready, you have permission and your test file is safely backed up.
checks: You have a 6 to 10 shot list, a gear list and a schedule
People and places in your shoot have given permission
Your test clip is copied and checked

title: Use your camera well
outcome: Film a steady shot that is sharp and not too bright or too dark.
topics: Brightness: aperture, shutter speed and ISO
assignment: Film something indoors, outdoors and something moving. Watch each clip. Fix one problem and film it again. Share both versions.
evidence: You can spot a blurry, shaky or badly lit shot and fix it.
checks: Your subject is sharp
The shot is steady and not too bright or dark
You found a problem and fixed it in a new take

title: Frame your shots and film a sequence
outcome: Film a short activity with different shots that fit together.
topics: Space above heads and in front of faces
assignment: Film an activity in 5 to 8 shots. Include one wide shot, the action, and one close-up detail. Share your clips and shot list.
evidence: People can follow the activity and nothing important is missing.
checks: You have a wide shot, the action and a close-up
People can follow the activity from your 5 to 8 shots
Framing and shaking don’t distract

title: Work with the light you have
outcome: Make your subject look better by moving them or the light.
assignment: Film a shot where the light looks bad. Then move the subject, the camera or the light to fix it. Share the before and after.
evidence: The after shot looks clearly better and you can say why.
checks: The after shot looks clearly better
You say what change made it better
You moved the subject, camera or light safely

title: Record clear sound and guide a speaker
outcome: Record someone speaking clearly and help them feel at ease.
topics: Putting the mic close to the speaker
Recording a few seconds of quiet room sound
assignment: Record a 20 to 30 second introduction and some natural background sound. Listen back, find a problem and record again if needed.
evidence: The speech is easy to understand and you checked it before you left.
checks: The speech is clear and easy to understand
You listened back and re-recorded if needed
You gave the speaker clear, kind directions

title: Organise your footage
outcome: Set up an editing project without losing any files.
assignment: Copy your clips into named folders. Start an editing project, close it and open it again. Share a picture of your folders and project.
evidence: Your files are easy to find and your project opens without missing clips.
checks: Clips are copied and the originals are kept safe
Folders and the project have clear names
The project opens again with no missing clips

title: Make your first edit
outcome: Edit a short video with a clear start, middle and end.
assignment: Edit a 45 to 60 second video of your activity. Show it to someone, then fix one part that was confusing or too long. Share both versions.
evidence: A viewer can follow the activity and your second version is better.
checks: The edit has a clear start, middle and end
Important parts stay and mistakes are cut
Your second version is clearly better

title: Edit sound and music
outcome: Mix voice, music and sound so people can hear what matters.
topics: Music you are allowed to use
assignment: Add a voice, some natural sound and music if it helps. Share the finished video and say why you used each sound.
evidence: Music never covers the voice and sound changes are smooth.
checks: Music never covers the voice
Sound changes are smooth
You explain why you used each sound

title: Fix colour so shots match
outcome: Make simple colour fixes so your shots look like they belong together.
topics: Spotting shots that are too bright or dark
Spotting colour that is too warm or too blue
assignment: Fix three shots that don’t match. Share before and after pictures.
evidence: Your shots match better and you can say what you changed.
checks: Three shots now match better
Details are still easy to see
You explain each fix

title: Add titles and captions, then export
outcome: Export a video that plays well, with clear titles and captions.
topics: Watching the final file all the way through
assignment: Export your video with a title and captions. Watch the final file and fill in a short checklist.
evidence: The file plays, the text is easy to read and captions match the speech.
checks: The final file plays all the way through
Titles and captions are easy to read and correct
You filled in the checklist

title: Your pathway project
outcome: Use what you learned to make a short video in the style you chose.
topics: What makes your chosen style work
A simple message for that style
Shots you need for that style
assignment: Make one short video in your chosen style. Share the video, your plan and your original clips.
evidence: Your video fits the brief, with clear pictures, clear sound and a simple edit.
checks: Your video fits your chosen style
Pictures are clear and the voice is easy to hear
You shared your plan and original clips

title: Beginner final project
outcome: Make a new video on your own from start to finish.
topics: A new brief in your chosen style
assignment: Make a new 60 to 90 second video. Share your plan, shot list, original clips, project and final video.
evidence: Clear message, steady and sharp shots, clear voice and a final file that plays.
checks: Your video has one clear message
Shots are sharp and steady, and the voice is clear
You shared your plan, clips and a final file that plays

title: Story, audience and the look of your video
outcome: Plan two ways to film one subject and pick the best one for your viewer.
assignment: Plan one subject two ways, like a bakery as a founder’s story and as an advert. Pick one and explain why. Make a short sequence to test it.
evidence: You name your viewer and the pictures that help them understand or feel.
checks: You plan two versions for a named viewer
You explain why you picked one
Your pictures support the feeling or message

title: Write a brief and a creative plan
outcome: Turn a vague request into a clear brief and plan.
topics: Good questions to ask a client
What to include and what to leave out
assignment: A client says “make a video about our business”. Write a one-page brief, a creative plan and your research notes.
evidence: Your brief covers the goal, viewer, message, size of the job, limits and who says yes.
checks: The brief covers the goal, viewer, message and size of the job
Your plan explains the idea, structure, pictures and sound
Limits, sign-off and how to judge success are written down

title: Plan a shoot and manage risks
outcome: Make a shoot plan that someone else could follow.
assignment: Share your shot plan, schedule, gear list, budget, permissions and a backup plan. Then update the plan after one thing changes.
evidence: The important shots are protected and the plan still works when something changes.
checks: Your shot plan, schedule and gear list are realistic
Permissions and a backup plan protect key shots
The plan still works after one change

title: Keep your shots consistent
outcome: Film a sequence where brightness, colour, focus and movement stay consistent.
assignment: Film one sequence indoors and one in tricky outdoor light. Share camera tests and explain your settings.
evidence: Important details stay clear and shots don’t jump in brightness or colour.
checks: Brightness, colour and focus stay steady between shots
You explain the settings you chose
Details stay clear in tricky light

title: Shots that cut together
outcome: Film enough of the right shots to edit a clear sequence.
topics: Wide, medium, close-up and reaction shots
Moving the camera with a reason
assignment: Film an activity you can repeat, using a limited number of shots. Share your clips and a 45 to 60 second edit.
evidence: People can follow the action and every camera move has a reason.
checks: People can follow the action without explanation
You have wide, close, reaction and extra shots
Camera moves have a reason and the action matches

title: Light a scene on location
outcome: Shape light into a look you can repeat.
topics: Separating the subject from the background
assignment: Create two different looks for one subject with simple gear. Share clips, a light sketch and a still from each.
evidence: You can repeat the look and explain each choice.
checks: You made two clearly different looks
A light sketch and still explain each look
You can repeat the look when things move

title: Record interviews and direct people
outcome: Record clean speech and guide someone through an interview.
assignment: Record an interview and an activity. Also record room sound and background sound. Find and fix one sound problem.
evidence: Speech is clear and you fixed problems before you left.
checks: Interview speech is clean and clear
You recorded room and background sound
You found and fixed a sound problem on the day

title: Organise and sync for editing
outcome: Set up a project that you or someone else can reopen and change.
assignment: Organise your project, sync the interview sound and pick your best takes. Check that you can relink missing files.
evidence: Someone else can open the project and find what they need.
checks: Files are checked, named and in bins
Interview sound is synced with the picture
Someone else can open and use the project

title: Edit for story and pace
outcome: Edit and improve a video so its pace fits the message.
topics: Letting sound lead or follow a cut
assignment: Make a rough edit and try two different openings. Show it to others, then share a better version with notes on what you changed.
evidence: You explain your choices and the new version is clearly better.
checks: The edit follows a clear story line
The pace fits the message
You explain what changed after feedback

title: Sound design and mixing
outcome: Build a soundtrack where the important words are always clear.
assignment: Finish the sound for your project. Share a before and after, and check it on headphones and normal speakers.
evidence: Voices are clear and the mix sounds good on different speakers.
checks: Voices stay clear above music and effects
Sound edits are smooth
You checked the mix on headphones and speakers

title: Colour matching and look
outcome: Fix and match your shots, then add a simple look.
assignment: Share a fixed version and a styled version of your project, with before and after stills.
evidence: Shots match, details are clear and you can tell fixing from styling.
checks: Shots are fixed and match each other
Skin tones and details look natural
You show the fix and the style separately

title: Titles, captions and versions
outcome: Deliver a checked final video and a shorter second version.
assignment: Deliver your main video, a short version, captions and a quality checklist. Get feedback once and make the changes.
evidence: No missing parts, wrong names or caption mistakes, and the short version has a clear purpose.
checks: The main and short versions both meet the brief
Captions are correct and well timed
Your checklist shows no missing parts or mistakes

title: Your pathway project
outcome: Use your skills to solve a real problem in the style you chose.
topics: Editing and delivering for that style
assignment: Complete the project for your chosen style. Share your plan, original clips, edit and any extra versions.
evidence: Your work fits the brief and shows you can run a small shoot on your own.
checks: Your work fits the brief for your style
Your plan, shots and edit suit that style
You shared your plan, clips, edit and versions

title: Intermediate final project
outcome: Plan, film, edit and deliver a short video on a new brief, on your own or with a small team.
topics: A new brief in your chosen style
assignment: Share your production plan, main video, one extra version, your project and a short reflection.
evidence: The video fits the brief and you solved key picture, sound, permission and delivery problems.
checks: The video fits a new brief, made on your own
You solved key picture, sound, permission and delivery problems
You shared your plan, extra version and reflection

title: Creative direction and point of view
outcome: Develop a strong creative idea and explain why it fits the audience.
assignment: Develop two very different ideas for one brief. Share both plans, reference pictures, sound ideas, and why you chose one.
evidence: You explain your choice, the risks, and why the other idea fits less well.
checks: You developed two very different ideas
You explain why your choice fits the audience
You name the risks and the weakness of the other idea

title: Research and test your story
outcome: Check that your story is true, can be filmed and has enough material.
assignment: Share a researched plan. Test one key idea with a site visit, interview, test shot or rehearsal. Note what you learned.
evidence: You spot weak ideas and change the plan when the facts don’t support it.
checks: Research supports your story
You tested one key idea before filming
You changed the plan when the facts said so

title: Produce: budget, schedule and changes
outcome: Run a realistic production plan with clear roles and controlled changes.
assignment: Share a full production pack. Then deal with a change, like less time or a missing person. Note the effect on cost, time and quality.
evidence: The key results are protected and every change is clear to everyone.
checks: A full plan with budget, schedule and roles
You handled a change and explained the trade-offs
The key results stayed protected

title: Camera tests and workflow
outcome: Choose and test a camera setup that works from filming to export.
assignment: Test your camera setup in two conditions, from filming to export. Share the settings, results and limits.
evidence: Results are consistent and you find the real cause of problems.
checks: Your setup gives consistent results
You noted settings and tests in two conditions
You traced problems to their cause

title: Direct people and plan coverage
outcome: Guide people and cameras to capture everything the edit needs.
assignment: Direct a scene, demo or interview with several camera angles. Do it again with less time. Share your plans and clips.
evidence: Directions are clear, key moments are captured and nothing important is missing.
checks: Your directions are clear and people feel confident
Key moments are covered from several angles
It still works with less time

title: Lighting design and continuity
outcome: Design a lighting setup and keep it consistent as things change.
assignment: Plan two connected light setups. Change the location a little and adapt. Share sketches, stills and notes.
evidence: The look stays the same and you explain what you changed and why.
checks: Both setups share one look
Sketches and stills let you repeat the setup
You noted what changed and why

title: Reliable sound on set
outcome: Use a sound plan that protects important recordings.
assignment: Record a two-person talk or event with a main and a backup recording. Then fix a pretend failure using copies.
evidence: You find the fault, choose usable sound and plan a fix.
checks: You used a main and a backup recording
You found the fault using copies
You chose usable sound and planned a fix

title: Look after media and hand over projects
outcome: Keep a shared editing project safe and easy to recover.
assignment: Hand your project to another learner. Do a recovery test. Check the final edit uses the right files.
evidence: The handover works without extra help and the right files are used.
checks: Someone else can open your project without help
Your recovery test worked
The final edit uses the right files

title: Shape the edit and handle feedback
outcome: Shape a complex edit and handle mixed feedback without losing the main idea.
assignment: Make two versions with different structures. Show them, do two rounds of changes, and keep a log of feedback.
evidence: Changes make the video better and you can explain each decision.
checks: You compared two structures with viewers
Two rounds of changes improved the video
Your log explains each feedback decision

title: Final sound mix
outcome: Build a clean soundtrack and mix it for where it will be shown.
assignment: Finish the sound on a tricky scene. Share the mix, the separate sound parts and notes on any fixes.
evidence: The sound supports the story, voices are clear and you meet the loudness target.
checks: Voices are clear and the sound supports the story
Noise fixes don’t leave odd sounds
You meet the loudness target and share separate parts

title: Colour management and look
outcome: Keep colour under control and give mixed footage one look.
assignment: Match clips from different cameras and create an approved look. Compare the edit with the exported file.
evidence: The video looks consistent and you check any difference in the export.
checks: Clips from different cameras match
Your look is separate from basic fixes
You compared the edit with the final file

title: Versions, quality checks and archiving
outcome: Deliver a checked package that can be shared, changed and found later.
assignment: Share your main film, a shorter version, captions and a clear handover note.
evidence: Files meet the brief, names are clear and someone else understands the package.
checks: Files meet the brief and have clear names
You delivered a short version and captions
Someone else understands your handover

title: Your advanced pathway project
outcome: Lead a strong project in the style you chose, with real limits.
topics: Changes and delivery for that style
assignment: Complete an advanced project in your chosen style. Share tests, original clips, all versions and why you made key choices.
evidence: Your work meets the style’s standards and handles real limits well.
checks: Your work meets your style’s standards
You shared tests and reasons for key choices
You handled real limits without relying on costly gear

title: Advanced final project
outcome: Lead a production from brief to final package and keep your idea strong.
topics: A real or practice client brief
assignment: Share your plan, production pack, tests, clips, project, final versions, change log and a short case study.
evidence: You led the key work, kept the idea strong and delivered a package others can use.
checks: You led the production through problems
Your idea stayed strong through changes
You delivered a full package with a case study
